decision: Accepted: bitwise causal recurrence preserved, modest prefill gains in both measured precisions, fewer submissions and scheduled state transfers. Default sequential decode kernels unchanged.
design: Prepare both tokens for each head, multicast prepared data to state-update and finish workers.
Keep FP32 state on the update core between two temporally ordered calls to the existing vector WKV function. The second update aliases input/output state; preserve token-0 y separately.
Write final state plus both y vectors through a compact intermediate; finish both tokens with existing normalization and residual math.
The fused-value variant gathers first-layer value vectors at a 55296-float stride. No CPU arithmetic or copies added.
compilation: Short FIFO names initially failed pool segment drainer resolution; descriptive unique names compile.
Fused-value preparation exceeded program memory by 96–160 bytes with a two-iteration wrapper loop; noinline did not resolve it.
Two explicit calls to the same value-prepare function fit program memory without changing arithmetic.

state_dma_descriptor_payload.scope: Scheduled state payload derived from DMA descriptors, not measured bandwidth or total internal traffic. Auxiliary payload and host payload unchanged.

stage.validation: Regular and fused-value variants pass full state/arena bitwise comparison against two decode runs, FP64 state/y oracle using baseline-prepared vectors, reset/replay, input immutability and allocation guards.

whole_model_protocol.order: A/B/B/A per precision, serial NPU dispatch with profiling disabled

profile.scope: Host stage wall time including scheduling, program switches, DMA and compute; odd tail has separate decode_profile output.
profile.next_action: Recurrence and channel mix remain the largest host stage times. Investigate recurrence/output fusion to reduce program boundaries; these host timings alone do not establish switch cost, DMA bandwidth or compute utilization.

limitations: Decode measured means increase about 0.10% BF16 and 0.17% INT8 FFN+output with batched prefill enabled; no decode speedup claim.
Whole-model gain is smaller than isolated-stage gain.
Hardware limits for the whole model remain unproven.
